title: Multi-value --lora-path/--lora-scale produce a LIST that crashes when fed to scalar pipeline kwargs
detail: The CLI registers --lora-scale/--lora-path as repeated/multi flags (action=append-style), so args.lora_scale / args.lora_path arrive as a Python list. Several command modules pass this list straight into a scalar kwarg: profile hands args.lora_path to pipeline.generate(lora_path=...) (expects one path), faceswap wraps args.lora_scale into lora_scales=[lora_scale] producing a nested list [[...]], expansion assigns the whole list to scalar lora_scale, and workflow stuffs the list into RunConfig.lora_scale (a float dataclass field). All four are latent crashes that only fire when a user actually passes the flag along that code path — static checks miss them. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run re-flagged the SAME class in a new locus: --lora-scale registered action=append (list) in _shared.py leaks into VIDEO pipelines expecting a scalar float (video-relay/video-generate pass-through) — confirms the list-vs-scalar leak is NOT confined to image sub-actions but spans the whole CLI surface. Fix pattern: unwrap to a scalar at the boundary (or make pipeline kwargs accept lists consistently) in BOTH image AND video paths. Found via effort:low review-only scan.

title: A flag's required=True is NOT satisfied by its --alias when both share the same dest
detail: refine.py registers --input-image with required=True, then app/commands/_shared registers --input to the SAME dest (input_image). argparse only recognizes the original option string for the required check, so a caller using --input (the alias) is rejected as missing-required even though the value landed in the dest. Net effect: the --input alias is permanently unusable for refine. General rule: when aliasing an option via shared dest, set required=True on only ONE registration and never rely on an alias to satisfy a required flag. Found via effort:low review-only scan (2 of 13 findings, one scored high).

title: Frame-floor helpers that early-return on a mod predicate bypass the minimum-frames guarantee
detail: video-vbvr._adjust_frames returns frames=1 unchanged when (frames-1)%8==0 — the modulo predicate is satisfied by 1 (since 0%8==0), so the 9-frame minimum is silently bypassed for that input. Pattern: any floor/ceiling helper whose guard is a divisibility/mod check rather than a direct comparison (frames < MIN) can pass the boundary value straight through. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run re-flagged the SAME class in video-relay._adjust_frames: the already-aligned branch (frames already divisible) returns frames=1 unchanged with NO min-9 clamp, identical root cause in a sibling command module — confirms the mod-predicate floor bypass is a recurring cross-module pattern, not a one-off. Always express floors as explicit numeric comparisons (frames < MIN: frames = MIN), not as side-effects of a mod branch. Found via effort:low review-only scan.

title: A ternary expression used as a bare statement discards its value — correctness depends on side-effect ordering
detail: video-relay uses `x if cond else y` as a standalone statement (not assigned). The ternary evaluates only one branch and throws the result away, so any code that relied on BOTH branches' side-effects (e.g. shutil.move ordering) is fragile. Linters rarely flag it because it is syntactically valid. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run re-flagged the SAME class in video-relay._mux_audio_track: the fallback expression-statement does nothing — the ternary in void context is confirmed dead-code-on-one-branch, not just theoretical. Rewrite as an explicit if/else so the intended branch's side-effect is unambiguous. Found via effort:low review-only scan.

title: effort:low review-only scan surfaces genuine latent bugs with ~0 adversarial overturn
detail: Default cheap lane (lanes:[review,lint], fix.mode=review-only) reliably surfaces real latent bugs across runs. 2026-06-19 run: 13 findings, ALL 13 passed adversarial verification (0 overturned). 2026-06-20 run: 6 findings, adversarialUpheld=0 again. 2026-06-21T00-10 run: 9 findings, adversarialUpheld=0. 2026-06-21T02-22 run: 19 new findings, adversarialUpheld=0 AGAIN (3 high + 10 medium + 4 low; argparse-integrity(9) + correctness(3) + error-handling(3) + type-safety(1) + import-hygiene(1)). Takeaway: the low-effort review lane has a consistently high signal rate (≈0 adversarial overturn across FOUR independent runs, 47 findings total); run it routinely and only escalate to medium+fix when you want changes applied. Adversarial-verify on effort:low is near-ceremony here — consider skipping it to cut cost on routine scans. Note: many findings are RE-flags of the same locus across runs (frame-floor bypass, lora list-vs-scalar, bare ternary, subprocess asymmetry) — the defects persist because fix.mode=review-only applies no patches; the knowledge file now carries the stable IDs so a fix run can target them.

title: Findings cluster in command modules at the argparse→pipeline boundary; _shared.py is the single highest-density locus
detail: All findings live in app/commands/ modules where argparse args (lists, required flags, defaults) meet pipeline dataclasses (scalars, fixed kwargs) — the type-coercion/dest-collision/default-bleed seam. 2026-06-19: 13/13 findings in app/commands/*. 2026-06-20: 6/6 in app/commands/*. 2026-06-21T00-10: 9/9 in app/commands/*. 2026-06-21T02-22: 19 findings in app/commands/* plus _shared.py (the shared argparse registration helper) and run.py entry — _shared.py itself is now the single highest-density locus (argparse-integrity(9) dominated by _arg_registered private-attribute use / shared-flag machinery), confirming the boundary-layer hypothesis at a finer grain: the DEFECT LOCUS is specifically app/commands/_shared.py + the per-command add_args() that calls into it. Review focus on _shared.py + app/commands/* yields the highest bug density for this codebase. Lint lane (pyflakes/check-model/self-test) stays clean on code quality (pyflakesRealCount=0, checkModelOk=true, selftestOk=true across this run); the lint lane is a structural-integrity backstop, not a defect finder.

title: A hardcoded pipeline kwarg (False/None) or an omitted kwarg silently freezes/forgets a feature even if a flag exists upstream
detail: Two faces of the same trap, both in video-relay. (1) Hardcoded literal: temporal_upscale=False is passed as a literal to LTXVideoPipeline — not sourced from any arg or default; no --temporal-upscale flag is registered on the relay parser, so the code path is permanently unreachable from the relay subcommand even though the underlying pipeline and the non-relay generate path support it. (2) Omitted kwargs: relay's pipeline.generate(...) call drops audio_stage1_only, audio_cfg_scale, modality_scale, audio_path, audio_volume — the args exist upstream (the generate path threads them) but the relay copy never passes them, so relay silently runs with pipeline defaults instead of the caller's audio/modality settings. General trap: any kwarg constructed as a bare literal in a command module, OR silently dropped from a copy-pasted generate() call, decouples the feature from the CLI surface — the flag can exist (or be assumed to exist) while the behavior is frozen/forgotten. Fix: thread the value from args (default it in the defaults table, register a flag), diff the kwargs against the canonical generate path, or delete the dead capability so the frozen-False/missing-kwarg is honest. Found via effort:low review-only scan (high + medium).

title: A flag's default is duplicated across registration-order / inline magic-numbers / None-sentinels and the duplicates drift; first-writer-wins and None-sentinels poison the dest
detail: A flag's default has ONE source of truth (argparse) but is routinely DUPLICATED — in first-writer registration order, in inline literals, and in None-sentinels — and the duplicates drift. Three confirmed faces: (1) first-writer-wins: image-purify registers --seed default=42 (SeedVR2 noise) while canonical t2i seed default is 777; whichever sub-action's parser builds first wins. Same class: image-review --output (unguarded add, semantic conflict with purify --output). (2) None-sentinel poison: image-profile registers --seed with default=None as a sentinel — but because profile's parser is the FIRST/only writer on a shared dest across ALL image sub-actions on the unified parser, default=None leaks into every image sub-action's --seed, silently treating an explicit user --seed as None. (3) inline magic-number compare: 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run surfaced video-generate._apply_prompt_defaults magic-number comparing cfg_scale/stg_scale against the WRONG argparse defaults — the helper hardcodes the expected default inline rather than reading it from argparse, so if a flag's registered default changes the comparison silently drifts (the inline magic number and the argparse default are two copies of the same fact that can disagree). Root cause unifies all three: the source-of-truth for a flag's default is argparse, but it is duplicated and the duplicates drift. Fix: never re-state a default inline; resolve the value explicitly per sub-action at runtime from a fresh local (never store the sentinel in the shared dest); do not rely on registration order or on None-as-skip. Found via effort:low review-only scan.

title: Bare subprocess.run(...) without except FileNotFoundError / Timeout wraps a crash in an unhelpful traceback; asymmetric guarding (2nd call wrapped, 1st not) is the easy-to-miss form
detail: video-relay._extract_last_frame calls subprocess.run([ffmpeg,...]) with capture_output=True, timeout=60 but no try/except. If the ffmpeg binary is missing, Python raises FileNotFoundError deep in the subprocess call (not a clean 'ffmpeg not found' message); if it exceeds timeout it raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired. The code only checks result.returncode AFTER the call, so the exception type is never converted to a user-facing message. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run sharpened the trap: in the SAME helper the SECOND subprocess.run IS wrapped against TimeoutExpired but the FIRST is NOT — the asymmetric guarding (one call guarded, one not, in adjacent lines) is the easy-to-miss form of the bug. Pattern: any subprocess.run on a possibly-missing external binary (ffmpeg/ffprobe/CLI tool) must be wrapped — catch FileNotFoundError and emit a guided install hint, catch TimeoutExpired and degrade — and the wrapping must be uniform across all calls in the helper (don't guard the second and forget the first).

title: A handle released on the happy path (cap.release()) is leaked if any later line raises; try/finally is mandatory for cv2/file handles
detail: cv2.VideoCapture/VideoWriter (and any OS handle) opened then released only on the success path leaks the handle / leaves the file locked when any line between open and release raises. Confirmed across multiple command modules: video-segment opens VideoCapture, reads metadata, then calls cap.release() — but only on the success path; any exception between open and release (or in subsequent detect_scenes/scenes_to_timestamps calls that still reference the video) skips release(). video-restore opens BOTH cv2.VideoCapture and a VideoWriter without try/finally — a later exception leaks both handles. General trap: a happy-path release() is not resource safety. Prefer with/contextlib.closing (or try/finally) so the release is exception-safe. Found via effort:low review-only scan (video-segment low 2026-06-20; video-restore medium 2026-06-21).

title: A command module that fully implements the contract (PARSER_META/add_args/run) but is absent from COMMAND_NAMES is unreachable
detail: animate.py implements PARSER_META, add_args(parser), and run(args) — the full command module contract — yet 'animate' is NOT in cli.COMMAND_NAMES ([image, refine, upscale, caption, replay, video, import-lora, import-workflow, check-model, schema-defaults, schema]) nor in COMMAND_ALIASES. So build_parser never registers it, `run.py animate` is an unknown command, and the module is dead code that still type-checks as valid (no static analyzer flags it, because it is internally complete). Re-flagged TWO findings in the 2026-06-21T00-10 run (a low and a medium, both naming animate.py) — the orphan persists across runs, confirming it was not fixed. Trap: a module can pass every quality gate while being structurally unreachable. Guard: assert the module's name appears in COMMAND_NAMES (a one-line integrity test), or delete the stub. The repo already has test_selftest_integrity.py for a parallel case (deleted-test references); a COMMAND_NAMES-membership assertion is the analog fix. Found via effort:low review-only scan (low 2026-06-20; low+medium 2026-06-21).

title: Help text that advertises a default the argparse default doesn't match, or a duplicate flag whose guarded twin is silently skipped, misleads users and reviewers
detail: Two related argparse-integrity gaps surfaced in the 2026-06-21T00-10 run. (1) Stale advertised default: image-t2i's help string advertises default 640/960, but the argparse default is None (the sentinel pattern) — a user reading --help is told a value is preset when it is not, and a reviewer reading help text cannot trust it as the source of truth. (2) Guarded-twin divergence: image-workflow registers --film-grain / --sharpening WITHOUT the _arg_registered guard, while image-purify registers guarded copies of the same flags — the guard dedupes and silently keeps only the FIRST (purify's) registration, so the workflow-specific help text/defaults never take effect even though they look wired. The two are the same root cause: the help/default surface and the actual argparse registration surface have drifted apart, and nothing asserts they agree. Fix: treat help text as a contract — add an integrity test that parses --help and asserts each flag's advertised default equals argparse's actual default; and for shared flags, register in exactly ONE place (canonical t2i/_shared) and never re-add unguarded in a sub-action. Found via effort:low review-only scan (image-t2i low, image-workflow low).

title: _arg_registered uses parser._actions (a private argparse attribute) to detect prior registration — fragile across argparse versions
detail: app/commands/_shared._arg_registered checks whether a flag is already registered by scanning parser._actions for matching option strings. parser._actions is an undocumented private attribute of argparse.ArgumentParser; its shape/contents are not part of the stable API and can change across Python versions or argparse refactors. A registration-guard built on a private attribute can silently mis-detect (false-negative → duplicate-add crash; false-positive → flag skipped) after a stdlib upgrade. The robust check uses only documented behavior: wrap add_argument in try/except argparse.ArgumentError (the documented signal that an option string is already taken), or maintain an explicit set of registered dest/option-strings in the helper. Prefer the try/except-ArgumentError pattern — it relies only on argparse's documented behavior and needs no private-attribute access. Found via effort:low review-only scan (medium, _shared.py _arg_registered locus).

title: sys.path.insert(0, ...) in the entry module (run.py) matches the known KB 'sys.path.insert(0) in library modules' anti-pattern (milder in an entry module)
detail: run.py (the CLI entry point) calls sys.path.insert(0, ...) to make app/ importable. This matches the repo's existing KB guidance against sys.path.insert(0) manipulation. In an ENTRY module the risk is lower than in a library module (there is no caller whose sys.path gets polluted before its own imports), but the pattern still couples importability to CWD/launch path and hides the real packaging fix (a proper package install / pyproject.toml / console_scripts entry point). Prefer declaring the project as an installable package so run.py is reached via a console_script and app/ is importable without path mutation. Keep this distinct from the library-module variant (which is strictly worse because it poisons every importer). Found via effort:low review-only scan (low, run.py entry).

title: A loop body that reads args.input_image / args.audio (or any shared argparse arg) for every iteration aliases shared state across iterations instead of per-iteration copies
detail: video-generate's A/B variation generate() uses args.input_image and args.audio for ALL variants in the loop. These are argparse-level singletons shared across iterations: if any iteration (or the called pipeline) mutates the object in place (e.g. appends to a list field, sets an attribute, caches by identity), subsequent iterations see the mutated state — producing cross-variant contamination that is invisible when each variant is independent but catastrophic if a frame/image is cached by identity. The same trap applies to any cached/memoized object read from args inside a per-variant loop. Fix: deep-copy or freshly resolve the per-iteration inputs at the top of each loop body (copy.deepcopy(args.input_image) or re-read from the source), and never assume args.* is immutable across iterations. Static analysis rarely catches this because the read looks read-only. Found via effort:low review-only scan (medium, video-generate A/B-variation generate()).
